A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WebSTAR study. The main text, equations, all 12 tables, five figures, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison despite title and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original agent evaluations, filtering and thought-augmentation ablations, human grading validation, and StepRM experiments, with additional results in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the benchmark evaluations, ablations, grading analyses, and appendix results.

M1.justification: The rollout, thought augmentation, score-based loss masking, and StepRM training procedures remain unchanged. Calling StepRM a process reward model clarifies its already documented step-scoring role.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same OpenWebVoyager-derived training coverage and evaluate on WebVoyager, Mind2Web-Live, and Online-Mind2Web. Website exclusions in Appendix B are unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same methods, including trajectory-level filtering, UI-TARS-1.5-7B, OpenAI CUA, and o4-mini grading. Newly cited Digi-Q and GUI-Actor are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Model sizes, training settings, rollout limits, evaluation metrics, benchmark procedures, and website exclusions are unchanged. No new experimental protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: The thought-augmentation comparison, data-scaling study, grading validations, threshold ablation, score distribution, and HuggingFace failure analysis are retained without substantive revision.

E5.justification: Both versions report four evaluation runs per query and 95% confidence intervals in Appendix A/Table 11. Section 4.3 also retains five grading calls per step for the same 230-step consistency analysis.

E6.justification: Matched tables, plots, and qualitative findings retain their results. For example, Table 9 reports the same average Pass@1 values of 47.0% for the filtered 7B model and 30.0% for UI-TARS-1.5-7B.

T1.justification: The SFT objective, score definition, threshold mask, and masked training objective in Sections 2–3.2 are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same pipeline, dataset, performance, and StepRM claims. The process-reward terminology does not alter their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of filtering and thought augmentation, proposed future RL use, teacher-quality and SFT limitations, and the appendix explanation of HuggingFace failures remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v1 provides a CUAStepFiltering code link; v2 adds project-website and WebSTAR dataset links and changes the code destination to the WebSTAR repository. Implementation settings and the full appendix prompts are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds GUI-Actor (Wu et al., 2025) to the introduction and Digi-Q (Bai et al., 2025a) to the critic discussion in Section 5, with corresponding references. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 prefixes the title with WebSTAR, refines reward-model terminology to process reward model in several passages, and makes limited accompanying prose edits. The section sequence and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds a resource-link row beneath the title and reflows appendix displays, including Tables 9–12 and Figure 5. Table 7's caption receives the terminology update; visual encodings and display contents are retained.

improvement.justification: The added dataset and project links and updated code reference improve resource discoverability. More precise process-reward terminology and two relevant citations modestly improve clarity and context. The scientific evidence and limitations remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
